stories.headline: Colorado Senate Republicans elect Lisa Frizell minority leader for 2027 session
stories.summary:
Colorado Senate Republicans met Saturday to elect their leadership team for the 2027 legislative session. Sen. Lisa Frizell of Castle Rock, the current assistant minority leader, was chosen as minority leader to head the 11-member caucus.

Sen. Byron Pelton of Sterling will become assistant minority leader, and Sen. Janice Rich of Grand Junction will continue as minority whip. Sen. Scott Bright of Platteville was elected caucus chair, and Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer of Brighton will remain the caucus representative on the Joint Budget Committee, a role she has held since 2023.

Current Minority Leader Cleave Simpson of Alamosa is stepping down to join Gov.-elect Phil Weiser's administration as agriculture commissioner. Frizell said the caucus will focus on the cost of proposals, who will pay for them, and how to do better for residents, citing utility bills and small-business hiring as examples.

The 2027 session begins Monday, Jan. 11.

stories.headline: Opinion: Wadhams says Trump and Victor Marx drove Colorado GOP losses in 2026
stories.summary:
In a Denver Gazette column, longtime Republican strategist Dick Wadhams argues that the 2026 election in Colorado was a referendum on President Donald Trump and the GOP gubernatorial nominee, Victor Marx. He contends Democrats won largely because they were not Republicans.

Wadhams points to Democratic victories in the 4th and 5th Congressional Districts and the 8th District, and notes that Trump lost Colorado in 2016, 2020 and 2024. He says Republicans have not held a major statewide office since Sen. Cory Gardner lost in 2020.

He criticizes Marx's campaign, citing the candidate's claims about exorcisms, his past, and campaign finance issues, and says Marx's primary win over state Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer worsened the party's position. The column is an opinion piece reflecting the author's views.

stories.headline: Family of Metro State student killed in Auraria crosswalk demands accountability
stories.summary:
The family of Marco Antonio Bautista Delgado, an 18-year-old computer science student at Metropolitan State University of Denver, is calling for accountability after he was killed Wednesday while crossing the street to class. The collision happened around 11 a.m. at 9th Street and Auraria Parkway.

According to a Denver Police probable cause statement, witnesses said Delgado was in the crosswalk with the walk signal when a water delivery truck turned and struck him. Driver Connor Hinkle, 24, returned to the scene and was cited for careless driving resulting in death. Police said drugs or alcohol did not appear to be factors, and the Denver District Attorney's office will decide whether to file charges.

A family friend said relatives learned of the death from witnesses and social media rather than police, and that they have not received updates. Denver Police did not respond to questions about contact with the family. Hinkle was driving for Eldorado Spring Water, which issued a statement to Denver7. A GoFundMe has raised more than $12,000 to help cover funeral costs.

stories.headline: Woman shot in possible attempted carjacking in Aurora
stories.summary:
Aurora police are investigating a shooting early Sunday as a possible attempted carjacking. Just before 12:30 a.m., officers were called to HCA HealthONE Aurora for a walk-in gunshot victim, a woman with a non-life-threatening wound.

Police said the woman and her spouse had parked in the 900 block of South Yampa Street and were talking in their vehicle when someone pulled up behind them and fired a shot through the driver's side window. The couple drove directly to the hospital.

The department's Gun Violence Suppression Team took over the investigation, which remains ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to call Metro Denver Crime Stoppers at 720-913-7867.

stories.headline: Denver on track for one of its latest first snowfalls on record
stories.summary:
With no snow in Denver's forecast for the next week, the city is again on track to see one of its latest first snowfalls on record, according to the National Weather Service.

The warm, dry pattern has persisted into mid-November. Forecasters say recent trends point to much drier conditions across metro Denver and eastern Colorado, with temperatures staying above normal.

Fog and low visibility were expected Sunday morning before sunshine and a high near 59 degrees.

stories.headline: Aurora student among 32 Americans named 2027 Rhodes scholars
stories.summary:
Thirty-two Americans were named 2027 Rhodes scholars on Saturday, and an Aurora student, Elizabeth Koenck, is among them.

The group includes a college senior who wants to clean up debris pollution in Earth's orbit and a student who has researched the use of artificial intelligence in healthcare. The scholarship funds graduate study at the University of Oxford in England.

The winners have a variety of academic and personal interests, according to the Denver Post report.

stories.headline: Aurora Hooters to close as chain shutters more locations
stories.summary:
The Hooters restaurant in Aurora, Colorado, is set to close this month, according to reporting by The Denver Post cited in a national roundup of 2026 closures.

The Aurora closure follows other shutdowns of the chain, including its last locations in New York City in March and Jacksonville, Florida, and El Paso, Texas, in October.

The roundup lists Hooters among several retailers and restaurants that have closed locations this year, including The Children's Place and TJ Maxx.

stories.headline: Semiprecious cocktail bar to host alpine holiday pop-up in Denver
stories.summary:
Semiprecious, an internationally acclaimed Denver cocktail bar, will host a monthlong holiday pop-up called Gift Horse from Nov. 27 through Dec. 31.

The apres-ski, chalet-inspired pop-up will feature 11 new winter cocktails, handmade alpine decor by Denver designer Christine Leahy, limited-edition merchandise and games. Co-owner Mike Capoferri said the bar will recreate a European mountain town bar while keeping its high-tech approach to cocktails.

Design and merchandise were created by co-owner Jon Hartman and the team at WunderWerkz.

stories.headline: Broncos prepare to face Raiders after bye week
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos did not play in Week 10 because of their bye and return in Week 11 to face the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field at Mile High on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:25 p.m.

Mile High Report noted that the Broncos are 3-0 coming out of the bye under coach Sean Payton, crediting the time off he gives players. The game is expected to be notable because, barring injury, it will be the second career start for Raiders quarterback and 2026 NFL Draft pick.

Elsewhere in Colorado, the nationwide FAA ground stop affected college football teams, leading to an unconventional Colorado State walkthrough.

stories.headline: Rockies hire Tony Cougoule as Albuquerque Isotopes pitching coach
stories.summary:
The Colorado Rockies' Triple-A affiliate, the Albuquerque Isotopes, hired Tony Cougoule as pitching coach, Purple Row confirmed Sunday. He joins Pedro Lopez's staff alongside Craig Bjornson, who held the role in 2026.

Cougoule spent the last seven seasons in the Chicago Cubs farm system, most recently as pitching coach for Triple-A Iowa since 2024. Iowa posted a 5.90 staff ERA in 2026, the highest in the International League, and finished 63-82.

The move follows comments from Paul DePodesta that the Rockies would expand their coaching staffs.

topStory.headline: Trump Departs for Asia Trip Culminating in First Three-Way Summit With Xi and Putin
topStory.summary:
President Trump left Washington on Monday for a trip through Asia that begins in Manila and ends in Shenzhen, China, where he is expected to meet Thursday with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Senior U.S. officials describe it as the first-ever trilateral meeting among the leaders of the three countries, which hold the world's largest nuclear arsenals. The meeting will take place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. Trump will hold a bilateral meeting with Xi beforehand, but officials said he will not meet Putin one-on-one.

According to the White House and administration officials, Trump plans to raise nuclear arms reduction and the war between the United States and Iran. He does not intend to discuss Russia's war in Ukraine, and a U.S. official said Ukraine is not expected to be part of the talks, which has prompted concern in Kyiv that its fate could be decided without its involvement. Officials said they do not expect a concrete agreement and characterized the session as an initial conversation. The last U.S.-Russia nuclear arms control treaty expired in February, and the administration says any new accord must include China, which has shown no interest. The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute estimates China has about 620 warheads, compared with more than 5,000 each for the United States and Russia, and U.S. officials expect China to reach 1,000 by 2030.

The itinerary begins in Manila, where Trump is scheduled to attend meetings tied to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit, a Quad meeting with Australia, India and Japan, and a bilateral meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Marcos is expected to raise the South China Sea, where the Philippines and China have competing claims. Trump is also expected to sign a trade deal with Thailand. He will then travel to Shenzhen for an APEC leaders' dinner and multilateral meetings. Elon Musk will accompany Trump for parts of the China leg, with officials pointing to his business interests there, and some U.S. business leaders are expected at the APEC CEO Summit but are not part of the official delegation.

The trip comes after voters delivered a sharp rebuke to Trump's party in this month's midterm elections, and foreign leaders are watching for signs of diminished political standing. Trump has also shaken up his West Wing leadership and faces calls from some allies to dismiss Cabinet members, including the secretaries of Commerce and Defense. Officials said he hopes to counter the narrative of declining influence by announcing new commercial deals and asserting American priorities. Some observers have compared the three-way meeting to the 1945 Yalta conference, and a former U.S. ambassador to Malaysia, Edgard Kagan, said presidential foreign trips help a president change the narrative and show he remains in command.

The administration is also dealing with a scandal involving Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, who had an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, raising questions about espionage and U.S. technology exports. Officials said Trump does not intend to raise the matter with Xi, nor to discuss a renewed internal debate over further restricting advanced chip sales to China. One senior official said it is not something the U.S. plans to share with the Chinese at this time. Attention now turns to Thursday's meeting in China, where the outcome on nuclear arms, Iran and trade will indicate whether the talks lead to follow-on negotiations.
